PROTECTION
OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Buton Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of North Buton Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Buton.
-4-
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of North Buton Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children in the womb who become victims of violence as well as children in conflict with the law.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
-5-
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment/strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to family, or community who can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
-6-
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 13
(1) In order to provide services and protection to Women and Children from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Education Office, Youth and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives, SMEs and Manpower Office, Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registration Office, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Office, Community and Village Empowerment Office, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Resort Police, Kulisusu Palace Customary Institution, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Higher Education Institutions.
(3) Further provisions regarding PPT shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

L GENERAL
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their self-worth and dignity as well as to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28I paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, as well as the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in North Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children Victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for human rights, justice, non-discrimination and victim protection. The objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are to a) prevent violence against women and children; b) eliminate all forms of violence and exploitation against women and children; c) protect and provide a sense of security for women and children; d) provide services to women and children victims of violence, reporters, and witnesses; and e) facilitate and mediate domestic disputes to realize the integrity of harmonious and prosperous households.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in North Buton Regency.

CHAPTER VII
REPORTING
Article 25
(1) PPT reports the implementation of protection services for Women and Children victims of violence to the Regent.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 27
(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, customary institutions or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 23 (1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.
Article 24 Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are conducted in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection for Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with SPM established by the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

Article 20
(1) In carrying out service duties toward Women and Children victims of violence, PPT coordinates with the Sub-district PPT.
(2) The mechanism for implementing duties as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures, which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII
FUNDING
Article 26
Funding for the implementation of protection of Women and Children victims of violence, is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 18
(1) In carrying out its duties and functions, the PPT may coordinate with the Sub-district PPT, and competent parties in making efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children.
(2) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing the prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 22
Letter a What is meant by "quick" is immediate action taken without complications or with procedures made easier. What is meant by "safe" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, not disturbed, and served in a friendly manner, respecting and appreciating.
What is meant by "empathy" is action that appreciates, respects, loves, befriends, and brings happiness aimed at pleasing and calming the victim's heart.
Letter b What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.

3.4.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation only (a) defines “Rumah Aman” as a temporary residence (Pasal 1 angka 28) and (b) mentions “Rumah Aman/Rumah Singgah/dll” as examples of what the generic term PPT could refer to (Pasal 1 angka 25). It also says PPT must provide protection and may cooperate/network with “rumah perlindungan sosial atau pusat trauma” (Pasal 14 ayat (1) huruf d), but it does not mandate establishing/operating a shelter/safe house service for victims (no clause like ‘menyediakan rumah aman’ / ‘menyelenggarakan layanan penampungan’). Therefore a ‘Yes’ for a dedicated shelter/protection shelter is not clearly supported by the Indonesian text; the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the available content, suggesting the golden label is likely incorrect.

L GENERAL
Women and children are groups vulnerable to experiencing violence. All forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity, thus requiring legal protection to protect their self-worth and dignity as well as to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
This view is based on Article 28I paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, as well as the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right". The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through implementing protection policies for women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilitation for victims, pursuing effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and pursuing the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in North Buton Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children Victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for human rights, justice, non-discrimination and victim protection. The objectives of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are to a) prevent violence against women and children; b) eliminate all forms of violence and exploitation against women and children; c) protect and provide a sense of security for women and children; d) provide services to women and children victims of violence, reporters, and witnesses; and e) facilitate and mediate domestic disputes to realize the integrity of harmonious and prosperous households.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of services, assistance, guidance, supervision, reporting and funding for women and children victims of violence in North Buton Regency.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Buton Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of North Buton Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Buton.
-4-
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of North Buton Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children in the womb who become victims of violence as well as children in conflict with the law.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
-5-
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment/strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to family, or community who can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
-6-
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
